items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: Hall & Oates, Simon & Garfunkel, Roberta Flack, Donnie Hathaway, everybody. When I really look at the overall picture I’ve had more fun than a barrel of monkeys.

ctx.x: I mean they wanted you in that seat.

But see I didn’t know — you go by the reputation of the things that you hear, even before all these things happening. And for me I said oh, okay. It didn’t matter. It didn’t matter © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-

who the artist was as far as I’m concerned. An artist is an artist. You go in, you do your job, and you leave. Now if you’re lucky enough to socialize with them on the outside after the job is done, great, fine. But it is not a way of life. I enjoy the artists. I enjoy all the names. I enjoy all the unknown names. They pay me to come in to do a job. That’s what I’m going to do. I’m going to do the job, and I’m going to get out of your way.
